findings.title: Nitro's Stylus and JIT compilers use a Cranelift release inside the range of two October 2026 miscompile advisories, and no unprivileged account can reach either fault
findings.difference: Nitro runs Stylus programs as native code compiled on each node, and its JIT validator runs the WebAssembly replay machine through wasmer. Both compile with cranelift-codegen 0.129.1, which is the wasmtime 42 line. Wasmtime's advisories of October 2026 report that Cranelift before 43 can miscompile functions with more than 2^24 values (CVE-2026-115889, any architecture) and that aarch64 code with a br_table of more than about 256,000 targets jumps to the wrong place (CVE-2026-115893). The public Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain endpoints run linux-arm64 builds.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager is EVM bytecode and never runs through Cranelift: the interpreter loop of the fork sends only code with the Stylus prefix to ExecuteWASM (core/vm/interpreter.go lines 168-172 at 0e44603). A miscompile could only touch the PoolManager's funds indirectly, through a Stylus program that calls it, or through a validator that computes a different settled state. A Stylus program would need one function with more than 16.7 million SSA values or a branch table with more than about 262,144 targets. The 256 KB limit on a decompressed program rules out the first; it does not rule out the second, since a branch table with one byte targets can come within a few dozen entries of that count. What closes the hazard is that new programs cannot be activated at all: activationGas is 2^64-1 on all three chains. The replay machine that the JIT compiles is fixed by the consensus-v61 root, chosen by governance, and the one-step prover, which interprets WAVM without Cranelift, decides disputes.
findings.impact: None today. If governance reopens activation with a larger size limit, or ships a consensus machine with a function large enough to hit the overflow, nodes compiling with different backends could disagree on a Stylus call's result, which halts or splits the chain without taking any PoolManager funds by itself.
findings.preconditions: Chain governance raising the Stylus size limit or reopening activation, and a crafted program; or a governance-chosen replay machine with an oversized function.
findings.mitigations: Offchain Labs can move wasmer's Cranelift to 0.130 or later (wasmtime 43 and up, or a 48.0.7, 49.0.4 or 50.0.0 line for the aarch64 issue) before Stylus activation reopens. The deployer needs no action.

sources.supports: wasmtime 42.0.1 depends on cranelift 0.129.1, so cranelift-codegen 0.129.1 belongs to the wasmtime 42 line
Nitro v3.12.4 locks cranelift-codegen 0.129.1 and wasmer 7.1.0 (the master lock pins the same cranelift)

Stylus programs are compiled natively per node with singlepass or Cranelift, with a fallback to the other compiler on failure (lines 365-400) and a Cranelift retry after a native stack overflow (lines 55-60)
the decompressed Stylus program size limit is 256 KB from ArbOS 60 (line 43)

CVE-2026-115889 (24 bit value fields overflow, wrong value references, wasmtime before 36.0.19 and 37 to 42.x) and CVE-2026-115893 (aarch64 br_table with more than about 256,000 targets); secondary source
CVE record for the Cranelift value index overflow (found by search, its text was not fetched)

cleared.check: Opcode battery, targeted set, call semantics, storage and transient key folding, the deployed-bytecode scripts of sets 1, 2 and 6, and mined swaps, rerun on 2026-11-24 against the endpoints of state/networks.json.
cleared.result: Every vector and call semantics word is as specified, no slot aliases, sets 1 and 2 identical to Ethereum apart from Elysium script 189 (gas), set 6 equal to the reference interpreter on 703 of 706 with the known gas and length exceptions, and 15,902 mined swaps pass the tick relation with no unexplained pair. The math in src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-54, SqrtPriceMath.sol:219 and 252, TickMath.sol:61-63, TickBitmap.sol:20-67 and BitMath.sol:22 and 45 therefore gets the specified opcode results on these nodes.

cleared.check: holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 MulMod with a four limb modulus (reciprocal reduction, uint256.go lines 720-730) and udivrem for smaller divisors, which serve mulmod(a, b, not(0)) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, mulmod(a, b, denominator) at FullMath.sol:48 and the rounding remainder at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252: are there edge inputs where the node's result differs?
cleared.result: No. 21,712 vectors with remainders at 0, 1, m-1 and m-2, quotients at both ends of the range, and moduli with top limbs 1, 2^63, 2^63+1 and all ones, plus the moduli the code uses, match on all three chains, and a planted fault is caught. v1.3.2 is still the newest release (proxy.golang.org lists nothing later) and both the 0e44603 fork and the public nitro master pin it.

cleared.check: Jump destination cache on the running unpublished build (lead L-677): does a cached bitmap follow the address instead of the code?
cleared.result: No. In one eth_simulateV1 request per chain, address X held code with a JUMPDEST at offset 4, then in the next simulated block code of the same length where offset 4 is PUSH1 data, then the first code again. The jump succeeds, fails with invalid jump destination, and succeeds again, and a second address with the push data code fails throughout. The node behind each endpoint (rc.9+b72783f on 42161 and 4663) therefore keys the analysis by content within one process.

cleared.check: Opcodes that later instruction sets define (CLZ 0x1e from Osaka, which ArbOS 61 runs; DUPN, SWAPN and EXCHANGE 0xe6 to 0xe8 from the Amsterdam set the fork enables at ArbOS 70): can they change what the PoolManager executes?
cleared.result: No. A linear disassembly of the 24,009 byte runtime in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json finds none of these bytes at an instruction position, and no 0x49, 0x4a or 0x4b either. Only the trailer byte 0xfe at 23,996 is INVALID.

cleared.check: Memory and stack pooling in the fork at 0e44603 (core/vm/memory.go, stack.go): can a reused buffer leak bytes into a new frame's memory, which the PoolManager reads after MCOPY and return data copies?
cleared.result: No. memory.go and stack.go are byte identical to upstream go-ethereum v1.17.4. Free clears the whole used length before the buffer returns to the pool, and Resize only reslices into capacity that was zero when allocated.

cleared.check: Interpreter loop of the fork against upstream v1.17.4: does the multi-gas change alter an error path?
cleared.result: No. The dynamic gas call declares a new err inside the block (interpreter.go line 233) and tests it on the next statement before charging, so no error is dropped. The other changes are the Stylus dispatch (lines 168-172), contract push and pop hooks and gas bookkeeping.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses since cycle 11: Security Council emergency action of 24 May 2026, the Trail of Bits audit list of 2026, and the Wasmtime and Cranelift advisories of April and October 2026.
cleared.result: The emergency action concerns renounceRole on the Arbitrum DAO's L1 timelock, a governance path with no funds at risk and no relation to the PoolManager's owner, which is the alias of a different timelock. The 2026 audits (Stylus permissioned deployer, Glamsterdam gas parameters, OSP soundness guard and others) list no fault an ordinary account can use. CVE-2026-34971 (aarch64 heap access) and the October advisories reach Nitro only through Cranelift, which runs no PoolManager code (finding above).

cleared.check: Transient storage boundary in the simulation path (A1, src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39): is a TSTORE visible to the next transaction of a block?
cleared.result: No. A slot written to 7 reads 7 within the call and 0 in the next simulated transaction and block on all three chains.

leads.why: The running build is private; endpoint answers match the specification, but the text is unread.

leads.question: Does a later Nitro release move wasmer's Cranelift past 0.129.1 before Stylus activation reopens through the permissioned deployer that Trail of Bits reviewed on 6 November 2026?
leads.why: CVE-2026-115889 and CVE-2026-115893 sit in that compiler; with activation closed they cannot be reached.

leadResults.answer: v3.13.0 is still not tagged: raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for go.mod at v3.13.0, rc.9, rc.10, v3.13.1 and v3.12.5, and proxy.golang.org reports b72783f and v3.13.0-rc.9 as unknown revisions of github.com/offchainlabs/nitro, so the commit is absent from the public repository. Elysium still answers debug_traceCall only with an API key and reports vlocal+unknown go1.25.12, so no step trace was possible. Its endpoint does serve eth_simulateV1, and all opcode, script, jump cache and transient probes give the same answers as the two rc.9 endpoints.

For the property that matters, on the running build. The commit text is private, but a code swap at one address across eth_simulateV1 blocks shows the jump destination analysis following the code bytes on the rc.9+b72783f endpoints of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain and on Elysium: a jump into push data fails after the swap and succeeds after swapping back. Reorg and redelegation lifetime of entries could not be read; a stale entry would still describe the bytes of its own hash, as cycle 12 found at 0e44603.

Not answerable from public sources: proxy.golang.org, which fetches from the public GitHub repository, does not know b72783f, and the public go-ethereum fork master is older than the 0e44603 pin. Endpoint behaviour matches the specification on every vector and script, including 21,712 new integer library vectors.

Operator level. No public watchtower or challenger for the Robinhood Chain or Elysium rollups was found, and this session has no Nitro binary to replay batches. Both rollups still pin the consensus-v61 root 0xc10cd7ec...dc97.

Operator level. The endpoints of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain still report go1.27.3 in a build dated 2026-11-16, after the fixed toolchain was released. Sequencer builds are not published, and settled state is still computed by consensus-v61 built with go1.25.9.
Operator level. No Go toolchain is available here, so no SSA dump was made.

Elysium still requires an API key for debug_traceTransaction, debug_traceCall and trace_call, and no mainnet explorer for chain 99901 could be found (the Kinetiq explorer named in Alchemy and Chainstack docs covers the 99801 testnet). eth_simulateV1 is open, and callsem.py's rollback tests pass on this node, but no mined transaction with a reverted and then completed unlock was identified.
